Vreelandella arctica sp. (arc'ti.ca. L. fem. adj. arctica, referring to the Arctic Ocean, where the type strain was isolated).

Cells are Gram-negative, rod shaped and about 1.82.2m in length and 0.40.6m in width and have flagella. The colonies are round, opaque white, smooth and moist, with regular edges, no halo, a central bulge and a diameter of about 3mm. Growth occurs at 441C (optimum, 28C), pH 611 (optimum, pH 7) and 0.522% (w/v) NaCl (optimum, 68%, w/v). This species has the ability to degrade alkanes and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons and can grow with dodecane, hexadecane, naphthalene, phenanthrene, pyrene and benzo[a]pyrene as the single carbon source. In the API ZYM test, positive for alkaline phosphatase, esterase (C4), esterase lipase (C8) (weak), lipase (C14) (weak), leucine arylamidase (weak), valine arylamidase, cystine arylamidase (weak), acid phosphatase and naphthol-AS-BI-phosphohydrolase. In the API 20NE test, positive for denitrification, d-glucose fermentation, UREase, -glucosidase (aesculin hydrolysis), d-glucose, l-arabinose, d-mannitol, N-acetyl-glucosamine (weak), potassium gluconate, adipic acid and malic acid (weak). In the API 20E test, positive for citrate utilization and fermentation/oxidation of glucose (weak), rhamnose (weak), melibiose and arabinose. Positive for the utilization of dextrin (weak), d-cellobiose (weak), -d-glucose, d-fructose, d-galactose, d-fucose (weak), d-sorbitol, d-mannitol, d-arabitol, glycerol (weak), d-fructose-6-PO4 (weak), l-alanine, l-aspartic acid (weak), l-glutamic acid, d-galacturonic acid (weak), l-galactonic acid lactone (weak), d-gluconic acid, d-glucuronic acid (weak), glucuronamide (weak), l-lactic acid, citric acid, -keto-glutaric acid, D/L-malic acid, bromo-succinic acid (weak), -hydroxybutyric acid (weak), -hydroxy-D, l-butyric acid, acetoacetic acid (weak), propionic acid (weak) and acetic acid. The predominant fatty acids (>10%) are sum in feature 8 (C18:17c and/or C18:16c), C19:0 cyclo 8c, C16:0, C17:0 cyclo and C12:0 3OH. Q-9 is the major respiratory quinone. The predominant polar lipids are DPG, PE and PG.

The type strain R06ZXJ2T (=MCCC 1A08467T=KCTC 92631T) was isolated from the sediments collected in the Arctic Ocean. The DNA G+C content of the type strain is 54.4mol%. The GenBank/EMBL/DDBJ accession numbers for the 16S rRNA gene and the draft genome of strain R06ZXJ2T are OQ363179 and JBANSN000000000, respectively.

Cells are Gram-negative, rod shaped and about 1.92.2m in length and 0.40.6m in width and have flagella and lipids around. In the API 20NE test, positive for -glucosidase (aesculin hydrolysis), d-glucose, d-mannitol, potassium gluconate and malic acid. The predominant fatty acids (>10%) are C19:0 cyclo 8c, sum in feature 8 (C18:17c and/or C18:16c) and C16:0. Q-9 is the major respiratory quinone. The predominant polar lipids are DPG, PE and PG.

The type strain DY715-9T (=MCCC 1A12469T=KCTC 92628T) was isolated from the TVG surface sediment samples collected in the southwestern Indian Ocean. The DNA G+C content of the type strain is 54.4mol%. The GenBank/EMBL/DDBJ accession numbers for the 16S rRNA gene and the draft genome of strain DY715-9T are OQ363177 and JBANSO000000000, respectively.

Torulaspora lindneri (lind ne.ri. N.L. gen. n. lindneri, of Paul Lindner, named in honour of his contribution to the establishment of the genus).

Culture characteristics: After the growth on YM agar for 3days at 25C, colonies are white, butyrous, circular, slightly raised, with a smooth surface and entire margins. Cells are circular with a diameter of 2.55m. Budding is multilateral and pseudohyphae or true hyphae are not formed (Fig. 2a). After 1month in YM broth at 25C, sediment is present, but no pellicle is observed. After the growth on V8 agar for 15days at 25C, persistent asci are formed through conjugation between a cell and its bud or between independent cells, each containing one or two spherical ascospores (Fig. 2b).
Torulaspora lindneri strain CGMCC 2.7783T. a: Vegetative cells on YM agar at 25C after 3days. b: Asci with spherical ascospores and tapered protuberances on V8 agar at 25C after 15days. Bars: 10m.

Physiological and biochemical characteristics: Sugar fermentation: d-glucose (or weak), sucrose and maltose are positive, while raffinose, d-galactose, lactose and trehalose are negative. Carbon compound assimilation: d-glucose, sucrose (slow), maltose (slow), trehalose (weak), melezitose (or slow), inulin (or delayed) and -methyl-d-glucoside (weak or slow) are positive, while d-galactose, l-sorbose, cellobiose, lactose, melibiose, raffinose (various), soluble starch, d-xylose, l-arabinose, d-arabinose, d-ribose, l-rhamnose, d-glucosamine, methanol, ethanol (or weak), glycerol, erythritol, ribitol, galactitol, d-mannitol (or weak), d-glucitol, salicin, d-glucuronic acid, d-galacturonic acid, dl-lactic acid, succinic acid, sodium citrate dihydrate, inositol, hexadecane, N-acetyl-d-glucosamine and xylitol are negative. Nitrogen compound assimilation: l-lysine (or weak) and ammonium sulphate are positive, while cadaverine dihydrochloride (or weak), potassium nitrate, ethylamine hydrochloride and sodium nitrite are negative. Growth in vitamin-free medium, 10% NaCl plus 5% glucose medium (weak) and on 50% and 60% (w/v) glucose are positive. Diazonium Blue B reaction, urease activity, liquefaction of gelatin and production of extracellular starch-like compounds are negative. The growth on YPD agar at 30C and 37C (weak) is positive, and negative at 40C.

The holotype CGMCC 2.7783 (original number HE144P-2) was isolated from the bark of a chestnut tree collected from Guangshan County, Xinyang, Henan, China, in August 2023, and was deposited in a metabolically inactive state in the China General Microbiological Culture Collection Centre (CGMCC), Beijing, China. An ex-type culture has been deposited in the Japan Collection of Microorganisms (JCM), Koyadai, Japan, as JCM 36914. The GenBank/EMBL/DDBJ accession numbers for the sequences of the D1/D2 domain of strains CGMCC 2.7783 and KKU-PM21 are PP235589 and AB714269, respectively, and of the ITS region are PQ498696 and PQ528005, respectively. The Fungal Names number is FN 572228.

Comamonas trifloxystrobinivorans (tri.flo.xy.stro.bi.ni.vorans. N.L. neut. n. trifloxystrobinum, trifloxystrobin; L. pres. part. vorans, eating; N.L. part. adj. trifloxystrobinivorans, eating trifloxystrobin).

Colonies of strain J-3T are semi-transparent and smooth with irregular edges after incubation for 2days at 30C on TSA plates. The strain grows in the presence of 01.0%NaCl (w/v, optimum, 0.5%), at 1535C (optimum, 30C) and at pH 5.08.0 (optimum, pH 7.5) and degrades 59.9% of 75.0M trifloxystrobin. Growth is observed on TSA, LB medium, NA and R2A medium, but not on marine medium. In API 20NE assays, positive for reduction of nitrate to nitrite, -glucosidase, -galactosidase, urease, assimilation of caprate, adipate, malate, citrate and phenylacetate, negative for denitrification, indole production, d-glucose fermentation, arginine dihydrolase, gelatin hydrolysis, d-glucose, l-arabinose, d-mannose, mannitol, N-acetyl-glucosamine, d-maltose and potassium gluconate. C. mitsuokai subsp. mitsuokai (mit.su.okai. N.L. gen. n. mitsuokai of Mitsuoka, named after K. Mitsuoka, a Japanese microbiologist) is mesophilic and obligately anaerobic. Cells grow in chains of rods, with a cell size of 04m3.780.78m. It is non-motile and does not form spores. It can be cultivated in PYG for 2days at 37C under anaerobic conditions, with an optimal pH range of 67. As previously described by Kageyama and Benno [5], cells produce acid from glucose, mannose, galactose, fructose, sucrose, maltose, cellobiose, lactose and salicin. Fermentation of glucose produces mainly acetate, butyrate and lactate. Starch hydrolysis is positive, whilst aesculin hydrolysis is negative. The cells do not produce gas, indole or hydrogen sulphide, and they do not reduce nitrate or liquefy gelatin. The cell wall contains A1c-type peptidoglycan with an (l-Ala)-d-Glu-m-Dpm peptide subunit. Its cellular lipidome comprises a diverse range of saturated and unsaturated fats. The type strain of C. mitsuokai subsp. mitsuokai is strain RCA14-39T (JCM 10609T=CIP 106738T=DSM 15897T), isolated from human faeces.
The GenBank accession numbers for the 16S rRNA gene and the genome sequence of strain RCA14-39T are AB030224 and GCA_000173795, respectively.

C. mitsuokai subsp. tridentinum is mesophilic and obligately anaerobic. Cells grow in long chains of rods that have a mean diameter of 0.5m and a length of 3.5m, approximately. It is non-motile and non-sporulating, as C. mitsuokai subsp. mitsuokai. It can be cultivated in PYG for 2days at 37C in an anaerobic atmosphere; the optimal pH range is 77.5. Growth is enhanced by supplementation of maltose, sucrose, glucose, cellobiose and inulin. It produces acetate in the presence of glucose. The cellular lipidome mainly includes saturated fats, particularly for LPE, PE, LPG, PG and MGDG classes. The type strain of C. mitsuokai subsp. tridentinum is the strain CMD8551T (=DSM 118469T=LMG 33725T=CIP 112509T) isolated from human faeces collected from a healthy volunteer.

Emended description of the genus Homoserinimonas Kim et al. 2012 [17]: short rods to rods, with variable motility. They thrive in diverse environments from air to sediments and exhibit a broad pH range (410) and wide temperature adaptability (437C), with optimal growth around 2830C. Salt tolerance extends up to 10%. Major fatty acids are typically anteiso-C15:0, with species-specific variations (e.g., C19:0 cyclo 8c in Homoserinimonas sedimenticola). Their menaquinone profiles are predominantly MK-10 and MK-11, and the cell wall varies: from B2 with d-Orn to l-LysD-Glu types, indicating structural diversity. Polar lipids include DPG, PG and often glycolipids or unidentified lipids. All analysed species have a genome size of 2.8Mb, with G+C contents ranging from 64.1 to 67.9%.
The type species is Homoserinimonas aerilata Kim et al. 2012.

Emended description of the genus Salinibacterium Han et al. 2003 [19]: non-motile bacteria with irregular or curved rod-shaped cells. Members of this genus typically form yellow or red colonies, with the latter being methanol-soluble and insoluble in water. These bacteria exhibit a broad tolerance for environmental conditions, including a wide range of temperatures (037C) and pH (4.512), with species-specific optima. Salt tolerance varies across the genus, with some species able to withstand up to 14% NaCl, while others prefer much lower salinity. Fatty acids include anteiso-C15:0 and iso-C16:0, as well as menaquinones MK-11 or MK-10. Polar lipids in the genus include phosphatidylglycerol and diphosphatidylglycerol. The cell walls contain either lysine and ornithine or dl-diaminobutyric acid, depending on the species. The genome sizes range from 2.8 to 3.0Mb, with G+C contents ranging from 59.2 to 64.0 %.
The type species is Salinibacterium amurskyense Han et al. 2003.

Cells are classified as Gram-stain negative, rod shaped, non-motile, non-gliding and aerobic. Colonies are yellow-pigmented, circular and convex shape. Cells are ~1.84.4m in length and 0.40.6m in width. After 48h of growth at 25C on Reasoners 2A agar, colonies reach a size of about 11.5mm. Flexirubin-type pigments are absent. Cells can grow on Reasoners 2A medium at temperatures ranging from 4 to 37C (with an optimal temperature of 25C), in the presence of 00.5% (w/v) NaCl (optimal NaCl concentration being 0% (w/v)), and at pH 7.0. However, cells cannot grow on MacConkey and LuriaBertani agars. Both oxidase and catalase activities can be detected. Cells can hydrolyse starch, Tween 40 and Tween 80 but are unable to hydrolyse casein and carboxymethyl cellulose. Cells show positive activity for aesculin and weakly positive activity for -galactosidase (para-nitrophenyl-D-galactopyranosidase) hydrolysis in the API 20NE test. Cells exhibit alkaline phosphatase, esterase (C4), leucine arylamidase, valine arylamidase, acid phosphatase and naphthol-AS-BI-phosphohydrolase and weakly positive esterase lipase (C8), lipase (C14), cystine arylamidase, trypsin, -glucosidase and N-acetyl--glucosaminidase in the API ZYM test. Cells display a positive result for aesculin and glycogen but a weakly positive result for d-glucose, d-maltose, d-lactose, starch and gentiobiose utilization in the carbon utilization test API 50CH. The major fatty acids are iso-C15:1 G, iso-C15:0 and iso-C15:0 3-OH. The major respiratory quinone is MK-6. It contains high levels of neutral lipids (SE, DAG, Triacylglycerol and Free Fatty Acids), with ~70% of the total lipids detected by the HPLC-CAD assay. Notably, SE and PE are dominant neutral and polar lipids, respectively, of this isolated strain.

The type strain, TBRC 19031T (=NBRC 117006T), was isolated from water samples collected 0.30m below the surface and mixed with water from 0.30m above the riverbed of the Mekong River at the Chiang Saen hydrology station in Thailand. The GenBank accession number of the complete genome is CP174374.1, with corresponding RefSeq accession numbers NZ_CP174374.1 (nucleotide) and GCF_047038255.1 (assembly). The accession number of its 16S rRNA gene sequence is PQ578042.1.

Cells are aerobic, non-motile, Gram-stain-positive, catalase positive, oxidase negative and rod shaped (0.30.50.81.1m) (Fig. S3B). The strain is an obligately halophilic Actinomycetes, requiring 1.0% (w/v) NaCl for growth with an optimum at 3.0% and exhibiting no proliferation in NaCl-free media. This aligns with the minimal criteria for halophilism as defined by Oren [47]. Optimum growth occurs aerobically around 30C, at pH 7.0 and with 3.0% (w/v) NaCl. Colonies appear yellow, circular and opaque with a wet surface, smooth edge and a diameter range of 0.40.9mm after 3days of growth on BHIB under optimal conditions.

Their NaCl dependency suggests adaptation to hypersaline niches, likely involving ion transport systems and osmoadaptive strategies common in halophilic bacteria [48]. Based on these characteristics, we further compared their genomic features. Through NCBI prokaryotic genome annotation, we identified a multidrug and pH resistance gene cluster (Mrp ABCDEFG) of the cation: proton antiporter-3 (CPA3) family in strains MJ170T and MJ173. This cluster encodes the Na+/H+antiporter subunits ABCDEFG [49]. Research indicates that the Na+/H+ antiporters in Bacillus subtilis 168 and Bacillus halodurans C-125 contribute to salt tolerance and pH homeostasis [49, 50]. Annotation via the Transporter Classification Database (TCDB; http://www.tcdb.org/) detected Na+/H+ antiporters in all two strains. This suggests that the Mrp gene cluster in the two Georgiana strains may also encode Na+/H+ antiporters and play a role in salt tolerance. The schematic diagram of the Mrp gene cluster in strains MJ170T and MJ173 is shown in Fig. S7.

Additionally, secondary metabolite prediction identified ectoine biosynthesis genes in the type strain MJ170T. Ectoine, a canonical compatible solute in halophiles, confirms their capacity for synthesizing osmoprotectants  a hallmark of halophilic adaptation [51]. The associated gene information is detailed in Table S2, and the genomic arrangement is depicted in Fig. S2.

With the API ZYM system, enzyme activity is positive for esterase (C4) (weakly), esterase lipase (C8) (weakly), leucine arylamidase, valine arylamidase (weakly), naphthol-AS-BI-phosphohydrolase and -glucuronidase. However, the following reactions are negative: alkaline phosphatase, lipase (C14), cystine arylamidase, trypsin, -chymotrypsin, acid phosphatase, -galactosidase, -galactosidase, -glucosidase, -glucosidase, N-acetyl-glucosaminase, -mannosidase and -fucosidase. The type strain, MJ170T (=CGMCC 1.4698T=JCM 37420T), was isolated from intestinal faeces of C. atratus from the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau (PR China) and has a DNA G+C content of72.0 mol%. Amycolatopsis ponsaeliensis (pons.ae.li.ensis. N.L. fem. adj. ponsaeliensis, pertaining to Pons Aelius, the Roman name of Newcastle upon Tyne, where the species was characterized).

Upon GYM Streptomyces agar, the colony surface is a dark yellowbrown developing into a white colour as sporulation occurs, and the colony rear is a yellowgold colour. The colonies have a dry texture with a powdery appearance upon sporulation, and the colonies are small, with round or somewhat irregular form, with a flat elevation and white hyphal margins. Growth was observed between the temperature and pH ranges of 1228Cand pH 68, respectively, with the optimum being 28C and pH 7. According to the Biolog system, it tolerates up to 4% NaCl (w/v), but no growth was observed at 8% NaCl (w/v). Based on in silico chemotaxonomy, it may produce phosphatidylethanolamine and phosphatidylglycerol.

According to the Biolog system, it utilizes dextrin, d-maltose, d-trehalose, d-cellobiose, -gentiobiose, sucrose, turanose, d-raffinose, -methyl-d-glucoside, d-salicin, d-glucose, d-mannose, d-fructose, d-galactose, l-rhamnose, d-serine, d-sorbitol, D-arabitol, myo-inositol, pectin, d-galacturonic acid, l-galactonic acid--lactone, d-glucuronic acid, d-saccharic acid, citric acid, l-malic acid, bromo-succinic acid, Tween 40 and acetic acid, but not stachyose, -d-lactose, d-melibiose, N-acetyl-d-glucosamine, N-acetyl--d-mannosamine, N-acetyl-d-galactosamine, N-acetyl-neuraminic acid, 3-O-methyl-D-glucose, d-fucose, l-fucose, inosine, d-mannitol, glycerol, d-glucose-6-phosphate, d-fructose-6-phosphate, d-aspartic acid, gelatin, glycyl-l-proline, l-alanine, l-arginine, l-aspartic acid, l-histidine, l-pyroglutamic acid, l-serine, mucic acid, quinic acid, p-hydroxy-phenylacetic acid, methyl pyruvate, d-lactic acid methyl ester, l-lactic acid, d-malic acid, -hydroxy-butyric acid, -hydroxy-butyric acid, -keto-butyric acid, acetoacetic acid and sodium formate.

The genome of RTGN1T has a G+C content of 70.9% and was 11,990,019bp in length. It was predicted to contain 11,499 genes in total, of which 11,345 were protein coding with 8,221 of these producing a protein with a functional prediction. The draft genome, 16S rRNA gene sequence and SRA data of RTGN1T have been deposited in INSDC under the accession numbers JAPZLD000000000, OP727617 and SRR22101359, respectively. The IMG accession number for the fully annotated draft genome is 2974268288. This species was deposited within the Spanish Type Culture Collection (CECT) and the Centre for Agricultural and Bioscience International (CABI) under the accession numbers CECT 30870 and 507287, respectively.

Streptomyces sediminimaris (se.di.mi.ni.maris. L. neut. n. sedimen, sediment; L. neut. n. mare, the sea; N.L. gen. n. sediminimaris, of marine sediment).

An aerobic filamentous actinobacterium develops substrate and aerial mycelia with straight, branched, polysporous chains of spiny spores measuring 0.50.8m0.91.4m. Its phenotypic traits are strain-specific. The type strain grows well on ISP (27) media, forming colonies in shades from light orange-yellow to reddish-orange, and typically secretes yellow soluble pigments, except on ISP 6. Growth occurs at 2040C, pH 4.011.0 and up to 9% (w/v) NaCl. It utilizes l-arabinose, d-glucose, d-mannitol, d-mannose, rhamnose, d-xylose, maltose and sucrose as sole carbon sources on ISP 9 agar. Starch hydrolysis, nitrate reduction, milk peptonization and milk coagulation are positive in this species, while H2S production, tyrosinase activity and gelatin liquefaction are negative. Most enzymes tested on API ZYM show positive reactions, except for lipase and -glucuronidase. The cell wall peptidoglycan contains ll-diaminopimelic acid with glucose, mannose, ribose and rhamnose in whole-cell hydrolysates. The predominant fatty acids are iso-C15:0, anteiso-C15:0 and iso-C16:0 with MK-9(H8) as the major menaquinone. Its phospholipid profile comprises PE, DPG, PG, PI and PIM.

Two phenotypic variants are MCC20T (=NBRC 117131T=TBRC 19240T) and MCC57 (=NBRC 117132=TBRC 19241) isolated from mangrove sediment in Chanthaburi, Thailand. With its higher genome quality, the type strain is MCC20T. The genome assembly has a 9,180,064bp size with a DNA G+C content of 72.0 mol%. The GenBank accession number for this genome is JBJWOT000000000 with PQ658771 for the 16S rRNA gene.

Symmetrospora pini (pini. N.L. gen. n. pini, referring to Pinus, the plant genus from which the type strain was isolated).

On YM agar after 7days at 20C, the streak culture is salmon pink to red, butyrous, smooth and semi-glossy with an entire margin (Fig. 2a). In YM broth after 3days at 20C, cells are ellipsoidal to cylindrical (3.54.469.1m) and occur singly. Budding is lateral (Fig. 2b). After 1month at 20C in stationary cultures, a sediment and a ring are present. In Dalmau plate culture on CM agar, pseudohyphae and hyphae were not formed. Sexual structures are not observed in any of the strains or when strains are paired on the tested media after 6weeks at 17C. Ballistoconidia are not produced on CM agar. Glucose fermentation is absent. Glucose, lactose (delayed and weak), cellobiose (delayed and weak), d-xylose (delayed and weak), d-arabinose (weak), glycerol (delayed and weak), d-mannitol (delayed and weak), d-glucosamine (delayed and weak), d-glucuronate (delayed and weak) and glucono-1,5-lactone are assimilated as sole carbon sources. Inulin, sucrose, raffinose, melibiose, galactose, trehalose, maltose, melezitose, methyl--d-glucoside, salicin, l-sorbose, l-rhamnose, l-arabinose, 5-keto-d-gluconate, d-ribose, methanol, ethanol, erythritol, ribitol, galactitol, d-glucitol, myo-inositol, dl-lactate, succinate, citrate, d-gluconate, N-acetyl-d-glucosamine and 2-keto-d-gluconate are not assimilated. Nitrate (delayed and weak) and nitrite (delayed and weak) are assimilated as sole nitrogen sources. Ethylamine, l-lysine and cadaverine are not assimilated. Maximum growth temperature is 30C. Growth in vitamin-free medium is negative. Growth on 50% (w/w) glucose-yeast extract agar is negative. Starch-like substances are not produced. Hydrolysis of urea and Diazonium Blue B reaction are positive.

Holotype CICC 33601T was isolated from a leaf of P. massoniana collected in Sifangjing Village, Pingtang County, Guizhou Province, China, in February 2023. It has been preserved in a metabolically inactive state in the China Centre of Industrial Culture Collection (CICC), Beijing, PR China. The ex-type culture has been deposited in a metabolically inactive state in the Portuguese Yeast Culture Collection (PYCC), Caparica, Portugal, as strain PYCC 9982 (=NYNU 232201). The GenBank/EMBL/DDBJ/PIR accession numbers for the sequences of the D1/D2 domain of the LSU rRNA gene and the ITS region determined in this study are OQ851926 and OQ851927 for CICC 33601T and OQ851928 and OQ857286 for NYNU 232218, respectively. The MycoBank number is MB 857729.

After growth in YM broth for 1month at 25C, a ring and a sediment are formed. The streak culture is pale yellow-cream, glistening, butyrous and smooth with an entire margin after 1month of incubation on YM agar at 25 C. No hyphae or pseudohyphae are observed on CMA, potato dextrose agar (PDA) and YM agar. Additionally, sexual reproduction is not observed on CMA, MEA, Fowells acetate agar or PDA agar under the same conditions. The strain could grow (weak) at 30C but could not grow at 35C. Growth in YM broth with 50% (w/v) glucose and in the vitamin-free medium is positive. Growth in YM broth with 10% (w/v) sodium chloride is negative. Ethylamine hydrochloride, cadaverine, l-lysine, creatine (weak) and creatinine are assimilated as sole nitrogen sources, whereas nitrate and nitrite are not assimilated.

The holotype, CGMCC 2.5852T, was isolated from the flowers of Y. denudata collected from the Beijing Olympic Forest Park, PR China. It has been deposited in a metabolically inactive state in the CGMCC, Beijing, PR China. The ex-type culture has been deposited in the Biological Resource Center, NITE (NBRC), Japan, as NBRC 114206. The GenBank/EMBL/DDBJ accession number for the 26S rRNA gene D1/D2 domain and the ITS sequence of strain CGMCC 2.5852T are PQ811590 and PQ805397. Its taxonomic description has been registered in Fungal Names (FN572294).

Planosporangium spinosum (spi.nosum. L. neut. adj. spinosum, spiny, referring to the spiny spore surface).

Gram-stain-positive, aerobic, non-motile, catalase-positive, oxidase-negative and spore-forming actinobacterium. Globose spores with a spiny surface are produced on a short sporophore of the substrate mycelium. The colony colour ranged from vivid orangeyellow to yellow. Diffusible pigment and melanin production are absent in all tested media. The strain grows well on ISP2, ISP3, ISP4, ISP7, MBA, GYE, YSA and CZA media and moderately on ISP5, PDA and NA, with optimal growth at temperatures between 35 and 41C and at pH 67. The strain can tolerate 3% NaCl. Nitrate reduction and hydrogen sulphide production are negative. Hydrolysis of aesculin, arbutin, starch, Tween 20 and Tween 80 is positive, while hydrolysis of CM-cellulose, gelatin, guanine, hypoxanthine, skimmed milk, l-tyrosine, urea, xanthine and xylan is negative. Strain 12N6T utilizes dextrose, l-arabinose, cellobiose, d-fructose, d-galactose, d-glucose, glycerol, maltose, d-mannose, lactose, raffinose, sodium acetate, sodium propionate, sucrose, trehalose and d-xylose as sole carbon sources but does not utilize myo-inositol, d-mannitol, l-rhamnose, d-ribose, d-sorbitol and xylitol. l-Asparagine, glycine and l-histidine are utilized as sole nitrogen sources, while hydroxyproline, KNO3 and methionine are not. The whole-cell hydrolysates contain meso-diaminopimelic acid, and the whole-cell sugars are glucose, mannose, arabinose, xylose and ribose. The polar lipid profile consists of DPG, PE, PG and two unidentified phospholipids. The major cellular fatty acids are anteiso-C17:0, iso-C16:0 and iso-C15:0. The predominant MKs are MK-9(H4), MK-9(H6), MK-9(H8) and MK-10(H4). Mycolic acid is not detected in the cells.

The type strain is 12N6T=TBRC 19149T=NBRC 117121T, which was isolated from soils of peat swamp forest collected from Rayong Botanical Garden in Rayong Province, Thailand. The DNA G+C content is 71.6 mol%. The GenBank genome accession number and the GenBank of 16S rRNA gene sequence of strain 12N6T are JBLYUB01 and PV175756, respectively.

Dickeya ananatis (a.na.natis. N.L. masc. n. Ananas, generic name of the pineapple; N.L. gen. masc. n. ananatis, of Ananas, of the pineapple).

D. ananatis is a Gram-negative, rod-shaped, motile bacterium measuring 2.910.02m in length, with peritrichous flagella. It is fermentative and grows optimally at 28C on nutrient agar medium supplemented with 0.4% glucose and on Kings B medium, forming milky white colonies within 24h. This bacterium forms pits on the CVP medium within 2448h [33] and causes maceration of potato tubers, taro slices and pineapple leaves. D. ananatis sp. nov. is catalase positive, oxidase negative, pectinolytic and positive for nitrate reduction. D. ananatis sp. nov. is able to utilize sucrose, d-raffinose, d-melibiose, -methyl-d-glucoside, d-salicin, N-acetyl-d-glucosamine, d-glucose, d-mannose, d-fructose, d-galactose, d-sorbitol, d-mannitol, myo-inositol, glycerol, d-glucose-6-PO4, d-fructose-6-PO4, d-aspartic acid, l-aspartic acid, l-glutamic acid, l-serine, pectin, d-galacturonic acid, l-galactonic acid lactone, d-gluconic acid, d-glucuronic acid, methyl pyruvate, l-lactic acid, citric acid, d-malic acid, l-malic acid, bromo-succinic acid, acetic acid and formic acid as carbon sources. It shows inhibition at pH 5, or in the presence of 8% NaCl, d-serine, minocycline, nalidixic acid, potassium tellurite, aztreonam and sodium bromate. The type strain is unable to utilize the following carbon sources: dextrin, stachyose, N-acetyl neuraminic acid, d-serine, quinic acid, p-hydroxy-phenylacetic acid, d-lactic acid methyl ester, Tween 40, -amino-butyric acid, -hydroxy-butyric acid, -hydroxy-D, l-butyric acid, -keto-butyric acid and propionic acid. Enzymatic reactions tested with the API ZYM kit give positive results for alkaline phosphatase, esterase, leucine arylamidase, acid phosphatase, naphthol-AS-BI-phosphohydrolase, -galactosidase and -glucosidase. The type strain is able to utilize citrate, produces indole and acetoin and is able to hydrolyse aesculin; it is negative for urease. Assays for antibiotic susceptibility showed that D. ananatis sp. nov. A5410T is sensitive to 13 antibiotics including trimethoprim, kanamycin, bacitracin, cephalexin, hygromycin B, vancomycin, cefotaxime, tetracycline, spectinomycin, chloramphenicol, carbenicillin, penicillin and gentamicin. The highest sensitivity was observed for cefotaxime, carbenicillin and cefalexins. The D. ananatis sp. nov. type strain is A5410T (=ICMP 25020T=LMG 33197T) isolated from pineapple in Hawaii. Its genome size is 4.77 Mbp with a G+C content of 53.5mol% based on the genome sequence. Other isolates of this species were also obtained from pineapple in Hawaii (A5391, A6136, A6137 and A5611), and two strains, CFBP 1272 and CFBP 1278, were isolated from pineapple in Malaysia.

The 16S rRNA gene sequence is available in GenBank (OR271567). The type strain A5410T genome from a previous study can be found under CP040816 (BioProject PRJNA544764, BioSample SAMN11855518). The genomes sequenced in this study have been submitted to the database with the following accession numbers: CP040816, CP146223, CP146227, CP146228, CP146224, CP146225 and CP146226.

Chryseobacterium gossypii (gos.sypi.i. N.L. gen. n. gossypii. of Gossypium, referring to the isolation of the type strain from cotton field).

The cells are aerobic, Gram-negative, non-motile and do not form spores. They test positive for catalase and oxidase. The bacteria appear as straight rods and form yellow colonies with smooth edges on R2A agar. They grow at temperatures ranging from 20 to 45C, with an optimal temperature at 37C. The pH range for growth is between 5.0 and 10.0, with an optimum between 6.0 and 9.0. The cells can proliferate in the presence of 0%10% NaCl, with the optimal salt concentration for growth conditions being 1%. The following reactions are positive: nitrate reduction; glucose fermentation; hydrolysis of aesculin, starch, gelatin and p-nitrophenyl--d-galactopyranoside; fermentation of glucose, arabinose, mannose, N-acetyl-glucosamine, maltose and gluconate. The following reactions are negative: indole production; hydrolysis of arginine and urea; assimilation of mannitol, caprylic acid, hexanedioic acid, malic acid, citric acid and phenylacetic acid. Positive enzyme activities include alkaline phosphatase, esterase, leucine arylamidase, naphthol-AS-BI-phosphohydrolase and -glucosidase. Trace enzyme activities include lipase, -galactosidase and -glucosidase. The enzyme activities of lipase, valine arylamidase, cysteine arylamidase, trypsin, chymotrypsin, acid phosphatase, -galactosidase, -glucuronidase, N-acetyl-glucosaminidase, -mannosidase and -fucosidase are negative. The major cellular fatty acids are iso-C15:0, iso-C17:0 3OH, summed feature 3 and summed feature 9. Strain 1RM2T contains MK-6 as the respiratory quinone. The principal polar lipids include phosphatidylethanolamine, unidentified aminophospholipids and unidentified lipids.

The strain type is 1RM2T (=GDMCC 1.4437T=KCTC 102275T), isolated from continuous cotton field soil samples in Xinjiang. The DNA G+C content is 39.5mol%. The GenBank accession numbers of the 16S rRNA gene and whole-genome sequences of strain 1RM2T are PP663718 and JBGCUR000000000.

Description: The description follows that of Bvre and Henriksen 1967 (Approved Lists 1980) [41] with some updates [37]. Non-motile, rod-shaped bacterium that is both catalase- and oxidase-positive. It does not produce acids from glucose, hydrolyse Tween 80 or liquefy gelatin. While it lacks haemolytic activity, it exhibits weak DNase activity and can weakly reduce nitrate. It does not produce indole nor display esterase or acid phosphatase activity. The major fatty acids include C18:0 and C18:1 9c. Its genomic G+C content ranges from 43% to 46%.

Lwoffella (Lwoff.ella. N.L. fem. dim. n. Lwoffella, named in honour of Andr Lwoff, a pioneering microbiologist whose contributions significantly advanced the taxonomy of Moraxella and bacterial systematics).

Description: Non-motile bacterium with cocci or rod morphology. It is catalase- and oxidase-positive, but does not grow on MacConkey agar or produce acids from glucose. The bacterium lacks growth on minimal medium, haemolysis, proteolysis on Lffler slants and hydrolysis of Tween 80. It does not liquefy gelatin or show alkaline phosphatase activity. Nitrate reduction and DNase activity are present, while indole, phenylalanine deaminase, esterase and acid phosphatase activities are absent. Major fatty acids include C16:1 9 and C18:19. Its genome G+C content is 42.5%.
The type species is Lwoffella lincolnii comb. nov.

Microbacterium jiangjiandongii (jiang.jian.dongi.i. N.L. gen. n. jiangjiandongii, of Jiandong Jiang, Professor at the Institute of Materia Medica, Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences, for his contributions to the treatment of bacterial infectious diseases).

Cells are Gram-stain-positive, facultative anaerobic, nonmotile, catalase-positive, oxidase-negative and short rod-shaped (0.70.81.01.1m). Growth occurs at 1042 (optimum, 30), at pH 6.59.5 (optimum, pH 8.0) and in the presence of 05.0% (w/v) NaCl with an optimum of 1.5% (w/v). Colonies are yellow, circular, shiny and mucoid after cultivation on BHIB for 2days at 30. Negative for hydrolysis of casein, cellulose, gelatine and urea; nitrate reduction; and production of H2S and indole. Acid is produced from aesculin, arbutin, cellobiose, -fructose, -galactose, -glucose, -mannitol, -mannose, -turanose, -xylose, gentiobiose, glycogen, lactose, -arabinose, -rhamnose, maltose, N-acetyl-glucosamine, potassium 5-ketogluconate (weak), potassium gluconate, salicin, starch, sucrose and trehalose, but not from -adonitol, -arabinose, -arabitol, -fucose, -lyxose, -sorbitol, -tagatose, dulcitol, erythritol, glycerin, inositol, inulin, -arabitol, -fucose, -sorbose, -xylose, melezitose, melibiose, methyl --glucopyranoside, methyl --mannopyranoside, methyl --xylopyranoside, potassium 2-ketogluconate, raffinose and xylitol. Positive enzyme activity for acid phosphatase, esterase (C4), leucine arylamidase, N-acetyl--glucosaminidase, naphthol-AS-BI-phosphohydrolase, valine arylamidase, -glucosidase, -galactosidase and -glucosidase. Negative activity for alkaline phosphatase, cystine arylamidase, esterase lipase (C8), lipase (C14), trypsin, -chymotrypsin, -galactosidase, -mannosidase, -fucosidase and -glucuronidase. The major fatty acids are anteiso-C15:0, anteiso-C17:0 and iso-C16:0. The polar Ls are DPG, PG and one unidentified GL. MK-13 is the major menaquinone. The acyl type of the cell-wall muramic acid is glycolyl. The peptidoglycan amino acids include alanine, glutamic acid, glycine and lysine. The cell-wall sugars are rhamnose and ribose.

The type strain, zg-Y625T (=GDMCC 1.3931T=JCM 36203T), with a G+C content of 70.5 mol%, was isolated from the intestinal content of M. himalayana collected from Yushu County, Qinghai Province, China. The GenBank accession numbers for the 16S rRNA gene sequences of strains zg-Y625T and zg-Y843 are OP159396 and OP159393, respectively. The GenBank accession numbers for the genome sequences of strains zg-Y625T and zg-Y843 are CP126740 and JANJGX000000000, respectively.

Cells are Gram-stain-positive, facultative anaerobic, motile, catalase-positive, oxidase-negative and short rod-shaped (0.70.80.81.1m). Growth occurs at 1042 (optimum, 25), at pH 6.010.0 (optimum, pH 8.0) and in the presence of 07.0% (w/v) NaCl with an optimum of 0.5% (w/v). Metschnikowia ratanii (ra.tani.i. N.L. gen. n. ratanii is named in honour of Sir Ratan Tata, an Indian industrialist and philanthropist, for his charitable contributions, establishment of various institutes in India and funding of numerous research programmes worldwide).

After 3days on yeast malt (YM) agar at 25C, the cells are spherical to ellipsoid (2524m) and occur singly, in pairs or small clusters. Budding is multilateral. On YM agar after 10days at 25C, colonies are large, circular, cream-white, low convex and umbonate, semi-glossy and smooth surfaced with an entire margin (Fig. 2b). On Dalmau plates after 10days at 25C, no hyphae or pseudohyphae are observed. The sexual stage, i.e. asci and ascospore formation, was not detected on YM agar, CMA, Fowells acetate agar, 5% malt extract agar and YCBAS (Table S1) media after 2months of incubation of individual or mixed cultures at 25C; instead, germinating cells were observed. Fermentation of d-glucose, d-galactose, sucrose, maltose, lactose, raffinose and d-xylose was not observed (Tables 2 and S3). Carbon compounds assimilated: d-glucose, sucrose, d-galactose, d-trehalose, d-maltose, melezitose, cellobiose, salicin (weak), l-sorbose, d-xylose, turanose, methyl--d-glucoside (weak), methyl--d-glucoside (weak), ethanol (weak), glycerol (weak), xylitol, d-glucitol (weak), citrate, d-gluconate (weak), N-acetyl-d-glucosamine and 2-keto-d-gluconate (Tables 2 and S3). Nitrogen compounds assimilated: l-lysine, cadaverine and ethylamine-HCl. Nitrogen compounds not assimilated: d-glucosamine, l-proline, l-glutamic acid, -aminobutyric acid, nitrite and nitrate. Growth in amino acid free medium, 10% NaCl and 5% glucose and at 35C is positive (Tables 2 and S3). Growth is negative on 0.01% and 0.1% cycloheximide and at 37C (Tables 2 and S3). Urease activity is negative. Diazonium Blue B reaction is negative.

Fibrella aquatica sp. nov. (a.qua'ti.ca. L. fem. adj. aquatica, living in water).

Cells are Gram-negative, non-motile, rod-shaped and facultatively anaerobic. They measure approximately 2.64.0m in length and 0.60.9m in width. After cultivation on R2A agar at 30C for 4days, the strain forms convex, circular colonies with smooth, entire edges and reddish pigmentation. The cells exhibit robust growth on R2A agar but weak growth on NA. The strain can grow at temperatures ranging from 10 C to 35 C and at pH levels ranging from 6.0 to 12.0 and can tolerate up to 0.5% NaCl. Optimal growth occurs at a temperature of 25C, at a pH level of 7.0 and in the absence of NaCl. Catalase and oxidase reactions are positive. The cells can hydrolyze CM-cellulose but not starch, chitin, casein, Tween 20, Tween 80 and DNase. In the API 20NE test, the strain tests positive for aesculin and gelatin hydrolysis, as well as -galactosidase activity; however, it tests negative for nitrate reduction, indole production, glucose fermentation, arginine dihydrolase and urease. It also tests negative for the assimilation of d-glucose, l-arabinose, d-mannose, d-mannitol, N-acetyl-glucosamine, d-maltose, potassium gluconate, capric acid, adipic acid, malic acid, trisodium citrate and phenylacetic acid. The predominant cellular fatty acids (>10%) are summed feature 3 (including C16:16c and/or C16:17c), C16:0 and C16:15c. MK-7 is the major respiratory quinone. The polar lipids include PE, two unidentified lipids, four unidentified ALs, five unidentified GLs, three unidentified APLs and one unidentified APGL.

Strain GW2-5T (=KACC 23817T=TBRC 19128T) was isolated from a freshwater sample collected from Gimpo-si, Gyeonggi-do, Republic of Korea. The genomic DNA G+C content of the type strain is 51.5 mol%. The GenBank/EMBL/DDBJ/PIR accession numbers of the whole-genome shotgun and 16S rRNA gene sequences are JBGGWF000000000 and PP976588, respectively.

Corynebacterium rhinophilum (rhi.no'phi.lum. Gr. fem. n. rhis, nose; Gr. masc. adj. philos, loving; N.L. neut. adj. rhinophilum, nose-loving, referring to the site from which the strains were isolated).

Optimal growth on solid medium was observed on BHI agar with 1% Tween 80 with incubation aerobically at 37C in a 5% CO2-enriched environment. Colonies on this medium measure 24mm and appear creamy white, exhibiting a raised or umbonate surface. Optimal growth in liquid medium was observed in BHI broth with 0.2% Tween 80; growth in TSB with 0.2% Tween 80 was also observed. In biochemical testing, strains were found to have alkaline phosphatase activity and showed variable pyrrolidonyl arylamidase activity and nitrate reduction. Fermentation of d-glucose and d-ribose was observed in a single strain. The major fatty acids identified were oleic (C18:19c) and palmitic (C16:0) acids. The genome of strain MSK072 has a size of 2.57 Mbp and a G+C content of 58.8mol%.

The type strain, MSK072T (=DSM 118652T=JCM 37534T), was isolated from a nasal swab collected in October 2019 from a 39-year-old male adult in Durham, NC, USA (30.01401 N, 78.94002 W). Colony and bacterial morphology are typical of Pasteurellaceae. The bacteria appear as coccoid or pleomorphic rods, stain Gram-negative and do not demonstrate motility at 22 and 37 C. Catalase and oxidase tests are negative. Neither V-factor (NAD) nor haemin (porphyrin test) is required for growth. A fermentative reaction is observed in Hugh and Leifssons medium with glucose. Common reactions included positive reactions in tests for nitrate reduction, alanine aminopeptidase, phosphatase and acid from (-)-d-mannitol, (-)-d-fructose, (+)-d-galactose, (+)-d-glucose and (+)-d-mannose. Negative reactions are observed in Simmons citrate test, acid from mucate, malonate base, H2S/TSI (triple sugar iron), growth in the presence of KCN, methyl red at 37 C, VogesProskauer test at 37 C, production of gas from nitrate, urease, arginine dihydrolase, lysine decarboxylase, ornithine decarboxylase, phenylalanine deaminase and indole. Gas is not produced from (+)-d-glucose. Phenotypic results obtained with the genus are in accordance with those of Pasteurellaceae [15]. The fatty acid profile is available from the Culture Collection University of Gothenburg (CCUG). The major fatty acids (>5%) include C14:0, C14:0 3OH/C16:1 ISO I, C16:1 7c and C16:0 with minor amounts (<3%) of C12:0, C18:2 6,9c/C18:0 ANTE, C18:1 9c, C18:1 7c /12 t/9 t, C18:0 and C20:1 7c (https://www.ccug.se/strain?id=15566) (accessed on 14 March 2025). This profile is typical for members of Pasteurellaceae with the dominance of C14:0, C16:0 and C16:1 7c [15]. The polyamine pattern of the type strain of the type species NCTC 11411T mainly included 1,3-diaminopropane in addition to small amounts of putrescine and spermidine [6].
The type species is Alitibacter langaaensis.

Macrococcus equi (e'qui. L. n. equi, of a horse)

Cells are Gram-positive, catalase-positive, non-motile, facultative anaerobic cocci with diameters ranging from 0.6 to 0.9m (Fig. S6). Isolated colonies reach 3mm in diameter after incubation at 37C for 24h on TSA-SB under aerobic conditions and 0.2mm under anaerobic conditions. The colonies appear light grey to white, circular, smooth and non-glossy with an opaque appearance. Four strains were non-haemolytic, and one strain (18KM583) was haemolytic (Table 3).

The strains were able to grow aerobically and anaerobically at 18C, 37C and 43C, and in BHI broth containing 7%, 9.5% and 12.5% NaCl. Oxidase and catalase reactions are both positive, and DNase is negative.

The strains tested negative for L-pyrrolydonyl-arylamidase, methyl--D-glucopyranoside hydrolysis, -glucosidase, and for acid production from D-mannitol, D-ribose, lactose, D-mannose, D-xylose, and D-maltose. Acid production from D-trehalose and sucrose was variable (Table 3). The strains were negative for leucine aminopeptidase, alanine arylamidase, and L-aspartate arylamidase, whereas tyrosine deaminase activity was variable. Respiratory quinone type is MK-6 with traces of MK-7. The peptidoglycan type is A3 l-LysGly, and the dominant fatty acids include C14:0, C16:111c, C16:0 and C18:113c.

The designated type strain is 18KM445 (=DSM 118744; =CCOS 2124; =CCM 9438), which was isolated from horse skin. Complete genome sequences for strains 18KM445T, 18KM444, 18KM245, 18KM583 and 21KM1573 have been deposited in GenBank under accession numbers CP179735, CP179734, CP179731, CP179736 and CP179732, respectively.

Macrococcus animalis (a.ni.malis. L. gen. n. animalis, of a living being, an animal).

The cells of this species are Gram-positive, non-motile, facultative anaerobic cocci with diameters ranging from 0.9to 1.4m (Fig. S6). After 24h of growth on TSA-SB at 37C, colonies reached a diameter of 2mm under aerobic conditions and 0.2mm under anaerobic conditions. The colonies appear white, circular, smooth, slightly raised, non-glossy and opaque, with no haemolysis. The strains grow at 18, 37 and 43C under both aerobic and anaerobic conditions and in brain heart infusion (BHI) broth supplemented with 7.0, 9.5 and 12.5% NaCl. Catalase and oxidase reactions are positive, and DNase is negative.

The strains produce acid from sucrose, D-ribose and D-glucose, and hydrolyse methyl--D-glucopyranoside. They are negative for L-pyrrolydonyl-arylamidase and for acid production from D-mannitol and D-mannose. Variable reactions are observed for -glucosidase activity, acid production from D-trehalose, D-xylose, D-maltose and lactose, and for novobiocin resistance (Table 3). Enzymatic activities for leucine aminopeptidase, alanine arylamidase, L-proline arylamidase and L-aspartate arylamidase are negative.
The respiratory quinone is MK-6 (100%), the peptidoglycan type is A3 l-LysGly and the dominant fatty acids are C14:0, C16:111c, C16:0, C18:113c and antesio-C15:0.

The designated type strain is EM39E (=DSM 118743; =CCOS 2125; =CCM 9439), which was isolated from bovine skin. Additional strains of this species were obtained from the skin of healthy pigs and horses, as well as from bovine mastitis milk. Complete genome sequences for strains JEK85, EM39E, 18KM676 and 21M1142 have been deposited in GenBank under accession numbers CP179725, CP179727, CP179728 and CP179724, respectively.

Cells are Gram-negative straight bacilli, ~0.20.4m wide and 1.22.1m long, with a flagellum at one end of the cell. The type strain, MOP7T (=LMG 33635T; =CCUG 77916T), was isolated from the oral mucosa of a domestic dog in the city of Valdivia, Chile. The G+CDNA content is 37.6 mol%. Bacteria are positive for the utilization of 40 carbon sources including d-raffinose, -methyl-d-glucoside, N-acetyl--d-mannosamine, d-saccharic acid, d-galactose, citric acid and d-glucose-6-PO4. Positive for urease activity, aesculin hydrolysis and assimilation of mannose, mannitol, N-acetyl-glucosamine, maltose, potassium gluconate, malate, trisodium citrate and arabinose.

Bacteria are negative for hydrolysis of gelatin, -galactosidase activity, arginine dihydrolase, reduction of nitrates to nitrites, reduction of nitrates to nitrogen, indole production and fermentation of glucose. Bacteria do not assimilate capric acid, phenylacetic acid and adipic acid.
Predominant fatty acids (>10%) are C18:17c 11-methyl and C19:0 cyclo 8c.

The type strain does not elicit root nodules on plants of M. albus (white sweet clover), M. lupulina (black medic), M. sativa (alfalfa) or M. atropurpureum (Siratro).

The DNA G+C content of the type strain is 55.1 mol%, and the genome size is 5.07 Mbp. GenBank/EMBL/DDBJ accession numbers for the complete genome and the 16S rRNA gene sequence of the type strain are, respectively, CP088273CP088276 and EU928869.

The GenBank accession numbers of the draft genome sequences of strains FAM 1755T, CREA 4990, FAM 27665 and DSM 46279 are GCA_046127645.1, GCA_031629375.1, GCA_046127635.1 and GCA_046127655.1, respectively. The GenBank accession numbers of the 16S rRNA gene Sanger sequences of strains FAM 1755T, CREA 4990, FAM 27665 and DSM 46279, used for the control of genome purity, are PV031525, PV031526, PV031528 and PV031527, respectively. The accession numbers of the 16S rRNA gene sequences of strains FAM 1755T, CREA 4990, FAM 27665 and DSM 46279, extracted from genomic sequences and used for computing the 16S rRNA gene phylogenetic tree, are PV016861, PV016862, PV016863 and PV016864.

Colonies grown on 6% NaCl DSMZ media 574 with 1.5% agar or 1% gellan gum are 13mm, circular with entire margins, convex, opaque and smooth, becoming rough with increasing salt content. Colonies become white with age owing to the elemental sulphur deposition. Thiosulphate-grown liquid cultures drop to a pH of 4.85.8 with the cessation of growth. pH of both gellan gum and agar is lowered during growth, sufficiently to change phenol red dye indicator from red to yellow. Obligately chemolithoautotrophic. Electron donors include elemental sulphur, sulphide, thiosulphate or tetrathionate but not sulphite or thiocyanate. Eurypsychrophilic, with growth occurring from 2 to 37C (optimum 30C). Growth occurs from pH 6.59.5 (optimum pH 7.58.0). Obligately halophilic with an optimum of 6%w/v and a maximum of 20%w/v NaCl. Carbon dioxide is fixed using the CalvinBensonBassham cycle. Strains of the species encode cbb3-type cytochrome c oxidase genes but distinctively lack a complete set of aa3-type complex IV cytochrome c oxidase genes. The dominant respiratory quinone is UQ-8 and the predominant cellular fatty acids are C18:17c, C12:0 3OH and C16:0.

G+C fraction of genomic DNA of the type strain is 64.7mol%. Raw sequencing data, whole-genome shotgun assemblies and 16S rRNA gene sequences were deposited to GenBank (under the BioProject accession number PRJNA1112440) as SRR29198315 (LHSS19-1T)/SRR29198314 (GHLCS8-2), JBDODP000000000 (LHSS19-1T)/JBDODO000000000 (GHLCS8-2) and PP662266.1 (LHSS19-1T)/PP974673.1 (GHLCS8-2), respectively.

The type strain is LHSS19-1T=NCTC 15100T=DSM 117890T isolated from the top 10cm source sediment of the LH spring system, a sub-zero, hypersaline (24% w/v NaCl) perennial spring on AHI, Nunavut, Canada.

After 3 days on YM agar at 25 C, the cells are ovoid to ellipsoid (4635 m) and occur singly or in pairs. Budding is multilateral. Colonies are white, convex, smooth and opalescent. In yeast extract (0.5%)glucose (2%) broth, sediment, ring and pellicle were not formed after a month. In YCBAS agar, after 2 weeks at 25 C, pseudohyphae were observed (Fig. 2b). The holotype of Sp. cesarfonsecae sp. nov. is CBS 14235, which is preserved in a metabolically inactive state in the CBS Yeast Collection of the Westerdijk Fungal Biodiversity Institute. An isotype of Sp. cesarfonsecae sp. nov., UFMGCMY425, is deposited in the Collection of Microorganisms and Cells of Federal University of Minas Gerais (Colecao de Microrganismos e Celulas da Universidade Federal de Minas Gerais, UFMG), Belo Horizonte, Minas Gerais, Brazil. Strains can utilize l-arabinose, d-fructose, d-glucose, i-inositol, d-mannitol, d-melibiose, d-raffinose, d-rhamnose and d-sucrose, but not d(+)-trehalose. Produces melanin. The type strain WI04-05BT (=LMG 33822T=NRRL B-65737T) was isolated from common scab lesion of potato and causes raised lesion on potato tubers. A nearly complete genome assembly of strain WI04-05BT is available through GenBank accession JBMKLA000000000.

Basonym: Pseudomonas carboxydohydrogena (ex Sanjieva and Zavarzin 1971) Meyer et al. 1980.

This bacterium was initially described as S. carboxydohydrogena by Sanjieva and Zavarzin [14]. Subsequently, Meyer et al. [15] reclassified it to P. carboxydohydrogena in 1980. The description is based on previous literature [15]. This bacterium is able to use carbon monoxide during aerobic processes as the sole source of carbon and energy for growth [15]. The G+C content (mol%) is 62.5 (determined by whole-genome sequence analysis). The genome size is ~3.3 Mb. The GenBank accession number for the whole-genome sequence is GCF_029030725.1. The type strain is DSM 1083T (=ATCC 29978T=Z-1062T=JCM 12568T=VKM B-1334T), isolated from sewage, as initially reported by Sanjieva and Zavarzin [14] with phenotypic properties.

Marinivivus (Ma.ri.ni.vivus. L. masc. adj. marinus, of the sea, marine; L. masc. adj. vivus, alive; N.L. masc. n. Marinivivus, an organism living in the sea).

Cells are Gram-stain-negative and aerobic. Catalase is positive but oxidase is negative. The major cellular fatty acids are summed feature 8 (C18:17c and/or C18:16c), C19:0 cyclo 8c and C16:0. The sole respiratory quinone is Q-10. The diagnostic phospholipids were PG, PE and PC. Phylogenetically, the genus Marinivivus is a member of the family Geminicoccaceae. The type species is Marinivivus vitaminiproducens.

Marinivivus vitaminiproducens (vi.ta.mi.ni.pro.ducens. N.L. neut. n. vitaminum, vitamin; L. pres. part. producens, producing; N.L. part. adj. vitaminiproducens, vitamin producing).

Cells are Gram-stain-negative, aerobic, non-motile and short rod-shaped (1.01.51.53.0m). Strain can grow in the range of 437C (optimum, 28C), at pH 6.010.0 (optimum, 8.0) and in the presence of 08.0% (w/v) NaCl (optimum 34%). Good growth occurs on 2216E agar, TSA and ISP2, but weak growth occurs on CA media. Colonies are circular, pink and convex after incubation on 2216E agar for 5days. Cells are positive for catalase, but negative for oxidase. Positive for the activity of alkaline phosphatase, acid phosphatase, -chymotrypsin, cystine arylamidase, esterase (C4), esterase lipase (C8), leucine arylamidase, naphthol-AS-BI-phosphohydrolase, trypsin and valine arylamidase, but negative for the activity of N-acetyl--glucosaminidase, -fucosidase, -galactosidase, -galactosidase, -glucosidase, -glucosidase, -glucuronidase, lipase (C14) and -mannosidase. Positive for hydrolysis of aesculin and gelatin; activity of urease; and assimilation of l-arabinose, d-glucose and d-mannose, but negative for the reduction of nitrate to nitrite; indole production; hydrolysis of p-nitrophenyl--d-galactopyranoside; activity of arginine dihydrolase; and assimilation of N-acetylglucosamine, adipic acid, capric acid, malic acid, maltose, d-mannitol, phenylacetic acid, potassium gluconate and trisodium citrate. The major cellular fatty acids are summed feature 8 (C18:17c and/or C18:16c), C19:0 cyclo 8c and C16:0. The sole respiratory quinone is Q-10. The polar lipids comprise PG, PE, PC, three PLs and one AL. The G+C content of the genomic DNA is 68.8mol%.
The type strain SCSIO 64248T (=MCCC 1K08013T=KCTC 92503T) was isolated from the stony coral Fungia sp. collected from South China Sea. The GenBank accession num:Q

bers for the 16S rRNA gene and complete genome sequence of strain SCSIO 64248T are OQ859101 and CP122393, respectively. The genome is 4,965,597bp with one circular chromosome, which contains 5,067 genes, including 4,939 protein-coding genes.
